title: 1. What Builders Are Actually Building
label: PRODUCT STORY
kicker: A local-first mobility intelligence scaffold: open the dashboard, inspect transport layers, select a district, and explain an access score.

cards.title: Map the network
cards.body: Show metro and bus layers with fallback tiles when Azure Maps is not configured.

cards.title: Select a district
cards.body: Anchor every demo around Riyadh district records.

cards.title: Explain the score
cards.body: Turn nearby metro, bus, and event inputs into a replaceable score.

cards.title: Run without cloud
cards.body: Bundled sample data keeps the app useful before Azure is ready.

cards.title: Keep contracts stable
cards.body: The frontend and API use the same contract locally and in Azure.

cards.title: Swap the domain
cards.body: Replace data, scoring, or overlays while keeping the app shell.

cards.title: Visible data layers
cards.body: Show transit coverage, district context, and live event markers.

cards.title: Transparent logic
cards.body: The score formula is simple enough to explain live.

cards.title: Azure-ready path
cards.body: The same containerized app can move to Azure when ready.

cards.title: Can the city be read?
cards.body: Can open mobility data become district intelligence quickly?

cards.title: Can access be compared?
cards.body: Can the score become service access or walkability?

cards.title: Can the scaffold extend?
cards.body: Can the pattern support new urban intelligence tracks?

callout: Product thesis: prove the end-to-end build path first, then let teams make the domain model more ambitious.
